Lesson No. 199: Explanation of Verses

1 to 3

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"Al-hamdu lillahi fatiris-samawati wal-ard... innallaha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (1)". The surah begins with the praise of Allah. The whole theme of this surah is to turn the human heart towards Allah, to look at Allah's blessings, to revive awareness of Allah's mercies, and to direct man towards the wonders Allah has created among His creatures. The human sense is to be filled with awareness of these wonders, and the result is that man becomes engaged in the praise and glorification of Allah.

All praise is for Allah.

Al-hamdu lillah (35:1): "All praise belongs to Allah." After this, the attribute of Allah that points to creation and origination is mentioned.

Fatiris-samawati wal-ard (35:1): "The Originator of the heavens and the earth." He is the Creator of these great and awe-inspiring creations that we see above and below us. Wherever we are, and regarding the very small bodies and the bodies nearest to us, we have some knowledge. All these bodies are controlled by one law of nature, with perfect proportion and harmony. All these things move, and we can conceive of them only by putting a great burden on our minds. All these bodies, along with their greatness and awe-inspiring nature, move in their orbits in one direction with such precise and intricate proportion that if even a slight deviation occurred in this proportion, all these great bodies would collide with one another, shatter to pieces, the Day of Judgment would come about, and all of them would scatter like cotton flakes of bread.

The Holy Qur'an repeatedly points to this great creation of the heavens, and we pass over it without stopping to reflect and ponder upon it. What is the reason for this? It is that our sense has become stagnant. The strings of our intellect and understanding have become rusted, and even the strong strikes of the Qur'anic plectrum have no effect on them, and despite those strikes no melody emerges from them. The song that once came from hearts joined to Allah, who remembered Allah and were astonished upon seeing these signs of Allah's power, has ceased. The reason for this, and this is the major reason, is that we have become so accustomed to seeing this great universe that its wonders no longer appear as wonders to us. Its unparalleled beauty does not impress us, and its extremely intricate technology does not astonish us, unless we look at them the way someone sees them for the first time and is greatly amazed.

It should be remembered that for an open heart, a heart joined to Allah, there is no need for great knowledge to contemplate and reflect upon the positions and rotations of the stars in the sky, to see their size and greatness, to study their environment, to determine the relationship and attraction of some with others, and to know the size, movement and condition of each. A heart that is connected to Allah does not need great and deep knowledge. With ordinary attention, the beauty and splendor of this universe can be seen. These scenes are sufficient to create a melody within the strings of the mind of a God-conscious person. Look at the countless stars shining at night in a clear and pure atmosphere and clear weather, when the night is dark, the weather is clear, and each star is casting its light upon the earth. Then look at the morning, the emergence of the dawn's whiteness and the rising of the sun. Likewise, look at the sun setting behind the mountains and the red twilight. Then look at this small earth and its various positions and scenes. No traveller can exhaust these scenes, nor can one be satisfied by touring them. Rather, I would say, look at just one flower: its colour, its petals, its formation, and the arrangement of its colours. Glory be to Allah, the Best of Creators.

The Qur'an points to these matters here and there, to great scenes and also to small, commonplace scenes. If a heart alive to the wonders points to even one of them, then for a living, awakened, thoughtful person the study of a single thing or a single flower is sufficient for guidance, and even on the wonders within a single thing, a person cannot fulfil the right of Allah's praise and glorification.

Al-hamdu lillah ... wa rab' (35:1): "Praise belongs to Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who appoints the angels as messengers, having wings two, three, and four." In this surah, the subject under discussion is the messengers, divine revelation, and the descent of revelation. The angels have a very important role in it, because it is these angels who bring revelation from the heavens to the chosen messengers, and this conveying of messages from Allah to the messengers is a very important and very weighty task. This is why, after the great creations of this universe, the special mention of the creation of the angels occurs, because it is these angels who are the means of connection between the earth and the heavens. They are the link between the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the chosen servants of Allah, namely the messengers, and this conveying and means of connection concerns the important task of this universe, the mission of prophethood.

From the beginning up to here, the Qur'an has repeatedly mentioned the angels, but for the first time it describes their form. Previously, the nature of the angels and their assigned duties had been discussed, for example:

Wa man 'indahu ... la yaftaroon (Al-Anbiya: 19-20): "And those who are with Him do not turn away from His worship out of pride, nor do they grow weary. They glorify Him night and day, and they do not tire." And elsewhere:

Innal-ladhina 'inda ... wa lahu yasjudun (7:206): "Those who are near your Lord do not turn away from His worship out of arrogance, they glorify Him, and they prostrate before Him." (7:206)

Here a new point is stated about their created form: "having wings two, three, and four." This is an attribute for which there is no parallel, nor can we conceive of how their wings and feathers are. We can only believe in it in general, that their wings are such. We cannot form any definite conception of it, because whatever estimate we make will be erroneous, and detailed descriptions of their form are not found in authentic hadith either. Another attribute of theirs is mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an:

'Alayha malaikatun ... ma yu'marun (66:6): "Over it are angels, stern and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and who do whatever they are commanded." Here too their form is not specified. What comes in the hadith is only that the Messenger of Allah saw Jibril (peace be upon him) in his true form twice. One narration mentions that he had six hundred wings, but even this does not determine his form and appearance. Therefore, this matter is also one of the unseen knowledge.

They have two, three, or four wings, while humans have seen only the wings of birds. Therefore Allah says:

Yazidu fil-khalqi ma yashaa' (35:1): "He adds to His creation whatever He wills." Thus Allah's will is unrestricted, and He is not bound by the forms He has made Himself. In His creation we see countless forms, and many forms are still beyond our knowledge.

Inna Allaha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (35:1): "Allah has power over everything." This statement is very broad and very comprehensive. Therefore there is no need to determine any particular form. That is, all forms fall within the scope of Allah's power. Every change and transformation takes place under Allah's power.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 2 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ (35:2)

In this second verse of the surah, a different aspect of Allah's power is displayed; the first verse mentioned Allah's power. When this aspect settles into a person's thought and conduct, his concepts, his consciousness, his direction, and his standards of good and bad are also dyed in its colour, and his whole life is coloured by it.

This colour cuts a person off from all the forces of the universe and joins him to the power of Allah. It makes him despair of all the doubtful mercies of the heavens and the earth. It connects him only to the mercy of Allah and makes him its hopeful seeker. It closes all the doors of the heavens and the earth and leaves open only the door of Allah; it closes all the paths of the heavens and the earth before him and leaves open only the path of Allah. Before him it closes all the routes of the heavens and the earth and leaves open only the way of Allah.

The manifestations of Allah's mercy are many and countless. If a human being wished to record in writing only those mercies, namely the manner in which Allah created humans, the distinctive powers He placed within the self, and the honour He bestowed upon them above His other creatures, he could not reach their limits. Likewise, the way Allah made the human environment conducive for him; He subjected everything around him, above and below him, to him; and the favours He bestowed upon him, both those he knows and those he does not seek. These favours are countless and innumerable.

Allah's mercy is present even in things that are forbidden, and it is present in things that are permitted. The person upon whom the door of Allah's mercy opens sees this mercy in everything: in every condition, every environment, and every place. In his consciousness and in his surroundings, wherever he is and whatever his state, he sees it, even if he is deprived of all the blessings that people regard as deprivation. Conversely, every person upon whom Allah closes His door in everything finds himself deprived of this mercy. Such a person remains deprived in every condition, in every circumstance, and in every place, even if he apparently possesses the material goods that people consider prosperity. Many worldly goods are such that Allah's mercy is not included with them; they become a punishment from Allah. And there are many hardships with which Allah's mercy is included; these hardships themselves become mercy. Sometimes a person sleeps on thorns, yet Allah's mercy is upon him; those thorns become a soft bed for him. Sometimes soft and delicate beds become thorns for a person and become a cause of great torment. A person may be doing the most difficult work, and yet, because of Allah's mercy, he is living a life of ease, while for another that same ease is a calamity. Sometimes a person enters a frightening situation, and it becomes a source of security for him; and sometimes a person passes through stages without hardship, and those stages become a cause of his destruction.

With Allah's mercy, no constraint remains a constraint. Even if someone is in the darkness of a prison, or within the walls of destruction, or in severe afflictions, the mercy of Allah makes his situation spacious. Indeed, apart from Allah's mercy, all spaciousness is constraint, even when someone is living amid blessings and comforts, prosperous, and possessing every facility of life. When a person attains the station of inner tranquillity because of Allah's mercy, the springs of righteousness, contentment, and peace begin to flow from within him. Thus within the self, anguish, fatigue, weariness, and the painful sting of toil and hardship begin to disappear, even though they may be deeply rooted in the self.

The key of Allah's mercy is a master key for all doors. Through it all doors open, through it all small windows close, and all wrong paths are blocked. A person becomes free of anxiety. When the door of Allah's mercy opens, expansiveness, ease, comfort, and tranquillity are attained. It is a door such that when it opens, all beneficial doors and paths open, and all non-beneficial doors close. And when this door closes, all those doors, windows, and paths that are not beneficial open, and a person falls into constraint, distress, hardship, restlessness, and exhaustion.

Sometimes this bounty of Allah envelops a person; then, even if his life is narrow or his financial condition is not good, or his living and enduring conditions are poor, he has no concern. This bounty is indeed the mercy that brings permanence, comfort, and felicity. But when the door of this mercy is closed, and from another direction provision is abundant and every kind of goods keeps coming, it is of no benefit; rather, it brings constraint, harm, and wretchedness and misery. Wealth, property, health, strength, and grandeur also often become a cause of grief, sorrow, fatigue, and toil, if the hand of divine power withdraws its favour and mercy.

Sometimes Allah combines His mercy with the beauty of life and the worldly provisions. Then what happens? Comfort and tranquillity prevail everywhere. In the world there is luxury, and for the Hereafter there is complete preparation. Against such people, the hearts of the worldly-minded then fill with envy and rancour. But if a person is given wealth but with miserliness, he becomes deprived; or if wealth is given together with illness, he is still deprived of the blessings of the world. And sometimes the wealthy become rebellious, and their wealth is also destroyed.

Sometimes Allah gives a person children, and the mercy of Allah is included with those children. Then these children become the adornment of life; they become a cause of joy and felicity; and in the Hereafter they become a cause of further reward. They become righteous and good successors for that person. But if divine mercy is not included with the same children, then these sweet children become a burden, a bane of life, a cause of misery and anxiety. They deprive one of the night's sleep and destroy the day's rest. Allah gives a person health and strength. Now, if divine mercy accompanies this health and strength, it is a blessing: life is lived well, and the pleasures of life increase. But if divine mercy is not included with this health and strength, then this health and this strength become a bane of life. A healthy and strong person falls into calamity. He spends his health and his strength on those activities that prove destructive to that very health and strength. Along with the ruin of his spirit and his character, his Hereafter also is ruined.

Allah gives some people rank and station, and His mercy accompanies such people. This rank and station become a means of reform: peace is established in the land, and this rank and dignity become a means by which a person leaves behind good deeds and good traces that are the finest treasury for the Hereafter. But if Allah's mercy is not included with authority and rank, that person remains restless; he oppresses people, transgresses the limits, and adopts rebellion. He harbours intense hatred and rancour towards people. This very authority and rule become a source of enmity for such people, and such a person then does deeds by which he gathers for himself a very great store of fire in the Hereafter.

Deep knowledge, long life, and rank keep changing. It is rare that knowledge and gnosis benefit someone, and rare that a long life becomes blessed. Sometimes it happens that a short life is itself a cause of blessing, and very little wealth becomes a means of great felicity.

A community is also like an individual, and a nation is also like an individual. Under every condition and in every circumstance, and by reflecting upon examples, it is not difficult to draw a conclusion. The sign of Allah's mercy is that a person perceives Allah's mercy. Thus Allah's mercy then embraces a person, and the rain of divine mercy pours down; bounties and blessings descend. But the awareness that one is under Allah's mercy is itself the greatest mercy. For a person to be hopeful of Allah alone and to rely upon Him is itself mercy. To attach one's hopes to Allah in every matter and to trust in Him is mercy. And the real punishment is that a person should be hidden from Him, despair of Him, and doubt Him. This is a punishment that never even approaches a believer.

﴿Indeed, none despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.﴾ (12:87)

For one who seeks Allah's mercy, it is found everywhere and by everyone; it is not scarce for anyone. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) found it in the fire. Yunus (peace be upon him) found it in the darkness of the belly of the fish. Musa (peace be upon him) found it in the waves of the sea while he was a helpless infant. Then he found it in the palace of Fir'aun, though Fir'aun became his enemy and went out in search of him. The People of the Cave found it in the cave, while in palaces and cities they had been deprived of it when they made that decision.

﴿So take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy﴾ (18:16). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companion found it in the cave, while the disbelievers were pursuing them and had tracked their footprints until they reached the mouth of the cave. This mercy is received by every person who despairs of all other means, who has no hope left that any power other than Allah can save him, and who fully believes that now only Allah's mercy can save him, having left all doors behind and become a supplicant at the threshold of Allah.

Furthermore, this too is a reality: if Allah opens His door of mercy to someone, there is no one to close it; and when Allah closes His doors of mercy upon someone, there is no one to open them. Therefore, in the heart of a true believer there is no fear of anyone; no hope is placed in anyone; there is no fear of anything departing, and no hope in anything. There is no fear of a means perishing, and no assurance even of the presence of any means. The absolute will of Allah is the real factor. Thus, if Allah opens the doors of His mercy, no one can close them, and if He closes them, no one can open them. The matter lies directly in the hand of Allah. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise. He ordains such measures and destiny that no one has any power to withhold or to grant. Allah's giving and Allah's withholding are in accordance with His own mercy; rather, they are in accordance with His own wisdom, and behind every act of Allah there is a wisdom at work.

﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him.﴾ (35:2) There is no veil between Allah's mercy and people. People may seek directly from Allah; they may seek without an intermediary. The only requirement is that the servant turn his attention, obedience, hope, and trust towards Allah and cease all resistance to submission.

﴿And whatever He withholds, none can release after Him.﴾ This verse brings the human conscience to supreme tranquillity, makes human consciousness and imagination most distinct, and grants human values and standards a lofty measure. The human personality attains dignity and contentment. It is a short verse, yet it draws up an entirely new map for life. It gives human imagination and consciousness most firm values, values that have no wavering, no inclination, and are not affected by passing matters. Whether these influencing factors come or go, whether they are great or small, whether their origin is people, events, or things, these values are not affected by them.

This is a way of life. If this belief settles into human life, then a person stands before events, things, individuals, great powers, values, and circumstances like a mountain, firm and unyielding, even if jinn and humans together assail him all at once. None of these jinn and humans can close the door of Allah's mercy, nor, if it is closed, can they open it. Only Allah is the Almighty and the All-Wise.

At the dawn of Islam, Islam and the Qur'an produced exactly such a group of people. Allah Himself produced this group through the Qur'an under His own supervision, so that this group would be the hand of divine power. This group was to create, on this earth, the beliefs and concepts that Allah willed; to give life the values that Allah wished to establish; to bring about the conditions and circumstances that Allah desired; and, having established in the world a life, a practical life, that when we read of it today appears to us as a tale and a story, to depart. This group, which was the destiny of Allah, Allah would impose upon whomever He willed. Through it Allah consigned some nations to oblivion and established others, whichever Allah wished to erase or to raise up. This was because this group did not deal merely with the words of the Qur'an, nor did it discuss merely beautiful theories and concepts. Rather, it established the Qur'an in its lives in practice, and that group lived within the world of the Qur'an.

The same Qur'an is present among people today. This Qur'an can still produce such groups, which can efface nations from the face of the world and [...]

Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), commentary on Surah Fatir (35), verse 2 (part 2 of 2):

...raise up peoples. But this will happen only when Qur'anic concepts settle into the life of a group in a concrete, practical form, become established and current, and the Qur'an is seen moving and walking in the life of a group. People should be able to see it with their eyes and touch it with their hands.

Now I come to this: through this brief verse I have come to know that Allah's special mercy is upon me. When I encountered this verse, I was spiritually very dry, intellectually very constricted, psychologically very troubled, and held in difficult circumstances in terms of my body and my means. In such hard and severe conditions, I studied this verse. Allah brought me to the reality of this verse. This reality was poured into my soul. It is as though it is a pure drink (sharab tahur) that is permeating every vein of my body, and I am feeling it. This is a reality that I am perceiving; it is not mere imagination. This reality itself is a mercy for me, and this verse is itself expounding its own interpretation before me. It was a real and practical interpretation. Just as the secrets and subtleties of this verse were unveiled before me, so too the doors of Allah's mercy were opened before me. Before this, I had been reading this verse and I had passed by this verse many times, but today this verse is bestowing the overflow of mercy upon me. I am being satisfied with its meanings and implications. I am seeing the reality of this verse clearly. This verse is calling me, saying: "Come, I am here. I am the mercy of Allah, whose door opens only occasionally. Just look at the wonders of Allah's mercy."

Consider: nothing in my surroundings has changed, yet my perception has now given every thing a new colour. This is an immensely great mercy that comes upon someone. The doors of Allah's mercy open, just as the treasures of this verse opened for me. It is a blessing from Allah, and when it comes upon someone, a person tastes it. He lives within it, yet it is difficult for him to describe it. Likewise, it is not possible to put this feeling and this taste into writing. I have remained for a long time in this outpouring of Allah's mercy, feeling it and recognising it. In the most difficult circumstances of my life, this condition came upon me. Now my state is that I feel expansion, joy, satiety, freedom and unburdenedness. I feel freedom from everything, freedom from every anguish and every grief, and I remain in the very place where I was. It is the mercy of Allah that has opened its doors upon me. It is the bounty of Allah that is raining down upon me through this verse. This is a verse, just one verse of the Qur'an, yet it has opened a niche of light in a dark cell. It has made a spring of pure water flow in a dry place for my refreshment, and now I am advancing with great tranquillity, upon a most open highway, towards the pleasure of God. And in the blink of an eye, my suffering has been transformed into my life's comfort. Al-hamdu lillah, hamdan kathiran. "O Lord, who sent down this Qur'an as a mercy from Allah, a mercy and healing and guidance for the believers."

This was a flash of light during the study of the Word of God, which I have recorded in writing. Now let us return to the Surah. The allusions present in the first two verses are also present in the third verse. Mention is made of Allah's blessings and mercies upon people through them. Allah, besides whom there is no deity, owner, ruler and provider. It is said in a wondrous style that, despite acknowledging this truth, these people assign these powers to another deity besides Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 3:

﴿Yā ayyuhā al-nās...﴾ ... ﴿fa-anná tu'fakūn﴾ (35:3). There is not even any need to remind people of Allah's blessings, because these blessings are so clear and manifest that whoever looks at them, perceives them and touches them can see them. Yet people forget. These blessings do not remain in their memory.

Just cast a glance at the earth and the heavens, and at this universe that encompasses man: at every moment Allah is showering His bounties upon man.

The doors of sustenance have been opened for them. At every step there is a blessing; in every moment there is a new bounty. Facilities keep coming to man from the heavens and the earth, and they come from Allah, who is the sole Creator and Provider. Allah's bounty is universal, and from whom does it come? Even the most fervent polytheist cannot say otherwise.

Is anyone other than Allah, the Creator of the universe, sending down these bounties, blessings and mercies? When there is no creator and provider except Allah, then why do they not take heed, and why do they not render thanks to the Divine? Why do they not praise and glorify Allah, and why do they not turn their attention exclusively to Him, turning away from worship? There is no sovereign except Him. Why, then, do they turn away from believing in a God about whom there is no doubt?

﴿Fa-anná tu'fakūn﴾ (35:3) ﴿Yā ayyuhā al-nās﴾: "Where on earth are you being deluded?" It is a astonishing matter that intelligent people should turn away from a truth so clear and a reality so evident, one that provides them sustenance night and day. And what could be more astonishing than that people can neither deny the Lord of Majesty nor acknowledge Him?

These were three blows, very strong and sharp, struck upon the strings of intellect and reason, and the Surah begins so that people may listen attentively to the melody of the entire Surah. The teaching given to man in every verse transforms him completely and settles in his consciousness as a profound truth. These three blows are interconnected and well-proportioned, and they produce a single effect from different directions.

Lesson No. 200 at a Glance

The first lesson was on three fundamental truths of the universe: that the Creator and Originator of this universe is Allah alone; that the treasury of mercy is with Him alone; and that He alone is the Provider. In this second lesson, the Prophet (ﷺ) is consoled that he should not be distressed by the denial and rejection of these people. He should leave their matter, and their reaction, to Allah. And people are addressed with a forceful and loud voice that Allah's promise of the Resurrection is true, and that they should beware of Satan, because his very mission is to lead you astray from these great truths. All people are told what the reward will be for those who believe, and what the end will be for those who fall into Satan's deception. At the end, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is again guided that he should not wear himself out with distress and destroy his life. Guidance and misguidance are in the hand of Allah. This happens in return for people's deeds, and Allah is aware of their works.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 5:

Verses: "O mankind..." to "...companions of the Blaze" (5-6).

The promise of Allah is true and it will certainly come to pass. There is no doubt about it. When it is true, then truth is precisely that which comes to pass. Truth is not lost, nor is it nullified, nor does it become void; it does not change its course or its path. The real point is that the worldly life alone deceives man.

﴿So let not the life of this world deceive you﴾ (35:5). But Satan is busy deceiving day and night, so you should be careful and watchful against him.

﴿And let not the arch-deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ (35:5). Satan has declared that he is your enemy, and he also persists in his enmity towards you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 6:

﴿So take him as an enemy.﴾ Therefore, you too should regard him as your enemy. Do not incline towards him, and do not consider him your counsellor. Do not follow in his footsteps, for an enemy does not walk in the footsteps of an enemy. If he is wise, [then you should know that] an enemy never calls a person towards good, nor does an enemy desire the welfare and salvation of an enemy.

﴿He only invites his party to become among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ He is merely calling his followers along his own path so that they may become among the people of the Fire. Can any person of sound intellect decide to become one of the people of Hell?

This is an intuitive feeling. When a person keeps in mind that a battle is ongoing between himself and Satan, he gathers all his strength. He remains awake at all times and defends his self and his thoughts. He protects himself from the deceit and misguiding schemes of the enemy, and he stays alert against every whisper of temptation. He measures every new matter by the standards of Allah and His Messenger, so that he may determine whether it is truth or deception.

This is an intuitive state which the Qur'an wishes to instil in every conscience, namely, to remain ready at all times to guard against satanic whisperings and to adopt precautionary measures, just as a person or a nation remains vigilant at all times against its enemy and is always prepared to confront its mischief and harm. [This is] for protection against the enemy's mental and physical harm, and maintaining a state of readiness to plunge into any battle at any time. In order to further strengthen this caution, defence, readiness and precautionary measures, it is explained what the end of the disbelievers will be and what the end of the people of Islam will be.

The verse in question: "Those who disbelieve, for them is a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward" (35:7). After this, it is explained how Satan misleads a person, what Satan's activity and his deceptive stratagems are like, which door he opens through which every kind of evil comes, and how he leads a person far along the path of misguidance, so that no one returns from there.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 8:

Afaman zuyyina ... bima yasna'un (35:8)

The door to shirk and its key is that a person's evil deeds are made to appear good to him. Satan does exactly this: a person's evil actions are made attractive to him, and he regards wrongdoing as good deeds. The more evil acts he commits, the more he believes that he is doing good, and those deeds genuinely seem good to him. Such a person never even reviews his actions to see where he has erred, because he becomes certain that he makes no mistakes. He firmly believes that whatever he says and does is correct. He takes pride in his words and actions, and he becomes infatuated with his deeds. It does not even occur to him to reconsider any of his actions or to hold himself accountable. Therefore he never retracts any thought or action, for when someone believes he is doing good, how can he abandon it? Good deeds, after all, never cause harm.

Afaman zuyyina ... hasana (35:8): "Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he regards it as good, [equal to one who is guided?]" Here is the great calamity that Satan imposes upon a person, and this is the point to which Satan leads a person by guiding him. First he misguides him, then he casts him into the pit of destruction.

For the one for whom Allah writes guidance and goodness, He instills in his heart sensitivity, awareness, caution, and the habit of reflection. He is not heedless of Allah's plans, nor is he heedless of the fact that Allah can change a person's heart at any moment. He does not overlook human nature with its weakness, instability and fallibility, nor can he ignore humanity's innate deficiency and helplessness. Such a person keeps watch over his deeds at all times. He constantly holds himself accountable. He remains very sensitive about himself. He fears Satan at all times and always hopes for Allah's help and support.

This is the point of distinction and separation between guidance and misguidance, between success and ruin. It is a profound psychological reality, which the Qur'an depicts in these words:

Afaman zuyyina ... hasana (35:8): "Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he regards it as good, [a fitting end?]"

This is the example of the misguided person who has been ruined and who finally arrives at the evil end of destruction, and all of this happens because his evil deeds were made attractive to him. Due to this attractiveness he becomes conceited. Thus veils fall over his heart and eyes, and he cannot see the right path at all. Such a person cannot even do any good, because he regards his own deeds as good. Such a person cannot correct his mistakes, because he believes he cannot err at all. He cannot reform any corrupt action, because in his own estimation corruption cannot proceed from him. Such a person does not even stop at any limit, because he considers every step he takes to be reform. In short, this is the only work of Satan: it is the door of all corruption and, ultimately, the key to misguidance.

Here Allah asks: what limit could there be to the misguidance of the one whose evil deeds have been made beautiful to him, so that he considers them good? No answer is given, because whatever answer one gives would be the same answer. Can hope be held for the reform of such a person? Can this person be like the one who constantly holds himself accountable for his deeds and fears Allah? Can he be like those who fear Allah? In short, whatever answer is given to this question, it will be the same answer. This is a style frequently found in the Qur'an, but in it there is an indirect allusion to one of these answers.

Fa innal-laha yudillu ... 'alayhim hasarat (35:8): "Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills." Thus it is answered that upon the one for whom Satan makes his deeds attractive, misguidance is decreed. Allah has opened for him the path of misguidance; he has entered into it, and there is no hope of his return. It is Allah's prerogative to guide whom He wills and to misguide whom He wills, in such a way that whoever seeks misguidance receives misguidance, and whoever seeks guidance receives guidance. The nature of misguidance is that it makes evil deeds appear good, and the nature of guidance is that the one who is guided is cautious in every matter, fears, holds himself accountable, and this is the difference between guidance and misguidance. And since this is the decision...

Fala tadhhab nafsuka 'alayhim hasarat (35:8): "Do not let yourself expire in grief over them." This matter of guidance and misguidance is in Allah's hands, even if the one concerned is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself. Indeed, hearts are between the fingers of Allah, and Allah is Muqallib al-Qulub (the Turner of Hearts). In this way Allah consoles the Prophet ﷺ, so that his compassionate and tender heart may find rest, for he could not bear to see their misguidance, while he saw how dreadful their end would be. Therefore his heart surged with the desire that they would accept the truth he presented to them. This is human longing: everyone knows that a person wants everyone to accept what he himself loves. Allah has compassion for His Messenger ﷺ, for this burden on his feelings is unjust, since it is not within the power or capacity of the Messenger ﷺ to bring everyone to guidance; that task belongs to Allah.

All sincere callers (du'at) must go through this state. They see the importance, beauty and benefit of their call. On the other hand, the condition of the common people is that they turn away from it. They cannot perceive the beauty, benefit and excellence that the caller perceives. Because of this lack of perception, they do not benefit from this call. Therefore such sincere callers should hold fast to this guidance from Allah: they should devote their full strength to the call, then entrust the people to Allah. If Allah has not decreed the truth for a people, they should leave them to their state and not despair.

Inna-llaha 'alimun bima yasna'un (35:8): "Indeed, Allah knows what they are doing." It is He who distributes guidance and decrees misguidance for whomever He wills. All these matters occur in accordance with His knowledge and His wisdom. Allah knows these things even before they have occurred; He knows in advance that it will happen. He has made this distribution from His eternal knowledge. But Allah does not punish on the basis of His eternal knowledge; He punishes when the disobedience actually proceeds from them. Here the second lesson ends. There is a deep connection between this lesson and the first, and likewise a connection with the lesson that follows.

Lesson No. 201: At a Glance

This third lesson consists of a series of journeys. These journeys carry human thought through the vast expanse of this universe, and in these journeys the Quran makes man aware of the proofs of faith. The phenomena shown to man between these journeys are the means by which the Quran supplies arguments and proofs for the Islamic call.

These journeys come after a discourse establishing that the authority of guidance and misguidance belongs to Allah alone, and in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was instructed not to concern himself with the attitude of those who turn away, and to entrust their affair to Allah, who is fully aware of all their deeds. The theme of this lesson is that if anyone wishes to believe, let him look: the proofs of faith are scattered everywhere in this universe, free of any complexity. Yet if someone truly wishes to go astray, he will go astray while the proofs of faith surround him on every side.

Consider just one scene: this earth, after being utterly dead, becomes green, flourishing and radiant. Is there not in this a proof that people will be raised in the same way after death? Then man was created from clay and made in his present form into a most excellent creature. This too is a proof. Then each stage of human creation is a proof, and man advances step by step according to a most precisely determined plan, and this plan too is recorded in the Clear Book, and it is a proof.

Then two kinds of water remain separate within one and the same sea: one is sweet, the other is salty. This too is a proof. And within the seas there are further blessings of Allah, and in everything there is the greatness of Allah. Then the scene of night and day, entering into one another, increasing and decreasing. This too is a proof, and also a proof in the establishing of this system. The subjection of the sun and moon to a single system is also a proof and an argument.

All these proofs and arguments are scattered throughout this universe. It is Allah who is the Creator and Owner, and those who are regarded as deities besides Allah cannot create even a date-stone's skin. They neither hear nor respond. On the Day of Resurrection they will disown the worship offered to them, and they will pronounce that these people were astray, and that whatever lies beyond truth is error.

Lesson 201: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 9 to 14

"And Allah it is who sends the winds, and they raise clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive the earth thereby after its death. Such is the resurrection." (9)

This scene recurs repeatedly in the Quran when it presents cosmic proofs: the scene of the winds, the scene of the clouds, the scene of the seas. The winds drive the clouds; vapour rises from the seas. Warm winds lift the vapour; cold winds condense it and give it the form of cloud. These vapours and clouds then move through the currents of the winds, northward and southward, eastward and westward, in whatever direction Allah wills for them to move. Until they reach their destined place and rain down, and where rain falls upon dead lands, the land comes alive.

"So We revive the earth thereby after its death" (35:9): thus this miracle takes place. Yet it is strange that people remain heedless, and despite witnessing such miracles every moment, the resurrection of people seems improbable to them, although the gathering and scattering of the dead lie in their own hands in this world.

"Such is the resurrection" (35:9): the raising of dead humans to life will likewise take place. This is the simple method of argument of the Quran. In the same way, this process will occur easily, for there is no difficulty for Allah in it.

This scene is repeated again and again in the Quran during the presentation of cosmic proofs, because it is a scene everyone sees, and there is no justification for denying it before man. Moreover, this scene strongly shakes a person, provided he sees it, understands it, and his heart is alive. Whenever a person reflects upon this scene, it overwhelms his consciousness. It is also a beautiful and pleasing scene, especially in desert regions where a person burns in the wilderness. When suddenly a green and flourishing area appears, a person's gaze is captivated, though only yesterday, when no rain had fallen, this very area was a bare plain and a dry desert. The Quran's manner is to draw its proofs from scenes that man has already seen, though man passes through these scenes daily in utter heedlessness. The truth is that when a person reflects upon these scenes, he finds them to be miracles.

Now the discourse shifts from the subject of the revival of dead earth to the field of psychological consciousness. This change of subject may seem strange at first: what is the source of honour, elevation, strength and majesty? And honour and elevation are linked with the good word and the righteous word, for the righteous word also ascends to Allah, and righteous action also attains honour and exaltation; whereas in contrast, the evil word and evil action are brought low and head toward ruin and destruction.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 10:

من کان یرید العزۃ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ اولئک ھو یبور (10) "..."

Perhaps the connection between the plant life that rises from dead earth and the good word and righteous deed is this: both possess a pure life and a noble nature. Plants have a good life, and righteous deed and the good word are also a pure life. The connection between them is the same that is indicated in the verse of Surah Ibrahim, namely the harmony between the temperament of the universe and the temperament of Islamic life. In Surah Ibrahim Allah says:

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly established and whose branches reach into the sky, giving its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord. Allah presents these examples so that people may take heed. And an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.﴾ (14:24–26)

This is a true likeness that exists between a pure word and a pure tree. Life and vitality exist in both. A word or idea also grows and bears fruit, and a tree also grows and gives fruit. Both share one and the same example.

The polytheists used to commit shirk so that their religious standing in Makkah would remain intact. Merely because of their creed and ideology, they were regarded as superior to other tribes. Moreover, they enjoyed material benefits. For instance, they were looked upon with respect, and because of this they were powerful and influential. This is why they used to say:

﴿If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.﴾ (28:57) Therefore Allah says:

﴿Whoever desires honour, let him know that all honour belongs to Allah﴾ (35:10). When this truth settles in a person's heart, his values and his standards of good and evil change. The means and plans for attaining those values also change.

The truth is that all honour belongs to Allah, and no part of honour belongs to anyone other than Him. If someone seeks honour, he should know that if he seeks it at that door, he will certainly reach it and will surely obtain it; and if he seeks it at some other door, he will be humiliated, because ﴿indeed honour belongs entirely to Allah﴾. The Quraysh, because of their idolatrous creed, sought honour from people. They feared accepting guidance in opposition to the people, although they thought that what Muhammad ﷺ called to was guidance. They feared that their standing and status would be diminished. The common people and tribes they feared did not have any source of honour; they were not owners of honour. The owner of honour is Allah.

﴿Indeed, honour belongs entirely to Allah﴾. If the Quraysh were strong, the source of strength is also Allah. Therefore it is their duty to take honour, power and glory from their true source, not from people. These people themselves are seekers of honour, needy and weak. This is the first of the truths of the Islamic view of life. It is such a truth that once it settles in a person's mind, it completely changes his values and his standards of good and evil. It changes the decisions and destinies of nations, their way of life and conduct. They change their means and resources. We should only fix this truth in our minds and then stand against the whole world. Then we will attain a dignified, honourable and lasting position in the world. Our weight will count among the nations of the world. This is the way of honour and dignity, and for a Muslim there is no other way.

When this truth settles in a heart, that heart no longer bows before any tyrant or oppressor. It does not fear any violent storm. No great calamity can destroy its resolve. No situation and no government can influence it. No kingdom and no expediency can influence it. No force of this earth can bow it down, and why should it be so? Since the source of every kind of power is with Allah, and no one else has any power.

This is why the good word and righteous deed are mentioned here:

﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾ (35:10). After this great truth, the commentary carries a specific meaning and indication. The indication is that if someone wishes to attain honour, what are its means? They are the good word and righteous deed. The good word rises directly to Allah, and righteous deed is lifted up to Allah. Thus Allah makes righteous deed honoured. This is why the possessors of the good word and righteous deed are always exalted, honourable and dignified, and honour is bestowed upon them.

True honour is that which, before it appears in this world or its signs appear, is settled in the heart of a person. When this truth settles in a heart, such a person steps outside the sphere of all causes of humiliation and subjugation. This is such a truth that when it settles in a heart, first of all a person gains control over his own commanding self (nafs ammarah). First he controls his base desires. When a person overcomes these human weaknesses, then there is no longer any cause to humiliate or subjugate him. What humiliates people is their desires and inclinations, fear and greed. The one who overcomes these weaknesses has in effect overcome all human beings. This is the true honour through which a person becomes exalted, strong and fearless.

Honour does not mean that a person is hostile to the truth, self-willed and rebellious, and strives to raise falsehood. Nor does strength mean that someone becomes sinful and wicked, a rebel and disobedient to Allah, and adopts disbelief with extreme obstinacy. Nor does strength mean that, while disobeying Allah, someone adopts a free indulgence in lust and shamelessness. Nor is strength that someone uses force without any principle or rule, and starts oppression without the aims of justice and reform. Never! Rather, strength is that a person gains mastery over his carnal desires. A person confronts humiliation and slavery, does not bow before anyone other than Allah, and humbles himself and submits only before Allah. He fears Allah, is wary of Him, and fears Him in both states of joy and sorrow. When someone attains such strength, his forehead will be raised, and such a person will be able to confront everything that his conscience does not approve. Such a person will not regard anything other than the pleasure of Allah. This is the station of the good word and righteous deed, in respect of honour and in relation to the connection of the theme of the discourse. After this, the counterpart of the passage is completed thus:

﴿As for those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment, and their plotting will perish﴾ (35:10). The word "yamkurun" includes the meaning of planning, but here makr is used in the sense of conspiracy and trickery, because it is most often used in a bad sense. For such people there is a severe punishment, and it is decreed for them that their schemes will perish; they will neither endure nor produce any result. The word "yabur" means "perish," and "bawr" and "buwar" have the same meaning. Since in the previous verse the indication was toward the cultivation of the earth and the bearing of fruit, here the word "yabur" is brought in contrast, in which the meaning is the destruction of fruit.

Those who engage in such schemes do so to attain false honour. They want that, in the eyes of ordinary people in society, they be honoured. Outwardly they want to appear as great people and men of honour, and appear powerful. Here honour is in a broader sense, but any evil scheme which lacks the good word and lacks righteous deed, its planner will never be honoured, dignified or powerful. Although sometimes he may establish his sway for a short time, in the end he moves toward destruction. This is Allah's promise, and Allah never breaks His promises. Yes, Allah does give every schemer respite, but when the time comes, all these deceptions perish.

Now, the first life and first creation of man is presented in another scene. In the previous scene it was described how Allah revives a dry earth through water and makes it green and flourishing. In the creation of man, its period in the womb of the mother, and then its long or short life span, all these things occur according to Allah's knowledge and plan.

And Allah created you from dust... ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ (35:11).

The Qur'an repeatedly points to the first creation of man, that he was created from dust. It also gives a detailed indication of the early stages of pregnancy, namely the drop (nutfah). Dust (turab) is the element in which there is no life, and the drop is the element in which there is life. One of the great miracles of this universe is how life was breathed into this lifeless element, and how life merged with the earlier element. To this day this secret remains a puzzle, and humanity has still not been able to reach it. It is an established and observed reality, and there is no option but to acknowledge it. This miracle drives a person towards Allah, the Creator, the Giver of life, the One of great power, and a person can in no form reject it, nor can he raise any objection in this field.

To transfer an element from the lifeless to the living is an extremely great revolution, and it is more significant than the distances of time and space. A person of a living heart, however much he reflects on this revolution, will never become despondent. Thus the secrets of this universe will never come to an end, and the secrets and mysteries that will be unveiled as knowledge advances on this path will each be stranger than the one before.

Now move forward a little from this drop. A single cell is completed, it becomes an embryo (janin), and then at a certain stage the sex of this embryo is determined: male and female, distinct from each other. Then there takes shape the form to which the Qur'an points:

﴿Then He made you into pairs﴾ (35:11). Whether this means that in the embryonic state the male and female distinction is made, or that after birth and after reaching maturity He made pairs through marriage, this revolution is itself sufficient to give thought and insight: that from a very small drop, male and female are formed in this way, and this too is a great revolution. Either it is a tiny point in the form of a drop, or it is a complete human being, a mighty creature, within whose body there are many machines performing various functions, whose details exist in the medical sciences and which are completely separate from one another.

Now, before us is this simple cell. It divides, and then divides again, and from it other cells emerge. From this single cell, collections of cells are formed, organs develop, and each organ is assigned its own function. A human being comes into existence from the combination of all these organs, and all of his organs are interconnected and in harmony. This human being is a completely distinct creature. He possesses characteristics different even from his fellow human beings, and indeed he is separate even from his close relatives. It is impossible for two human beings to be exactly alike, although they came from the same drop, and no one was aware of any difference within it. Then these cells take the form of male and female and become pairs, and through these pairs the continuity of this creation is maintained, and this continuity proceeds through these same stages. The same stages are repeated again. This is such a wondrous sequence that its marvels never end. For this reason the Qur'an repeatedly mentions this marvel. It is not one secret but a collection of secrets within the human body. If people reflect upon it, there are countless wonders in a single human body, and the human soul can awaken through reflecting upon them. This is why the Qur'an repeatedly shakes and awakens humanity from this angle.

After presenting this detailed study, a reference is also made to the vastness of Allah's knowledge. As the details have come in Surat Saba that Allah's knowledge is very vast, here too the creation of male and female, and pregnancy and childbirth, remain within His knowledge:

﴿No female conceives nor gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ (35:11). Now the scope of male and female is widened here. Humans, animals, birds, fish and all creeping creatures come within its scope, whether we know them or not, whether they give birth or lay eggs, because the egg is also a kind of pregnancy. The embryo inside the egg does not grow in the mother's womb, but grows inside the egg. Only the egg comes out of the mother's body. And this too is a wonder of Allah's craftsmanship: a process that takes place inside the womb is, here, carried out with this entire technology inside the egg, outside the body, and then it grows, and Allah knows all these processes, and His knowledge encompasses them. This entire universe has various dimensions.

This comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge is such that the human mind cannot grasp it, neither in terms of conception nor in terms of the manner of expression, as we explained in Surat Saba. This itself is proof that Allah is the One who revealed the Qur'an, that the source of the Qur'an is the vast Being of the Creator, and that this is a unique method of argument. Furthermore, the lifespan of various individuals and things is also within Allah's knowledge and recorded in the Book.

﴿And no one is granted a long life, nor is anything diminished from his lifespan, but it is all recorded in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ (35:11). When the mind turns to the fact that in this universe there are plants, birds, animals, humans and other things, whose sizes and dimensions differ, which are of various kinds, and which exist in different regions and times, then when a person considers that this great number, of which only the Creator has true knowledge, is each given a lifespan, whether that lifespan is long or short, whether it is increased or decreased, all of it is recorded in one Book, and Allah knows about all of them.

Indeed, Allah also knows about the part of each individual, what its lifespan will be, whether it will be longer or shorter. For example, what will be the lifespan of a leaf of a tree, when it will emerge, when it will fall, and when it will turn to dust. Allah knows about every feather of every bird, when it will separate from its body. Every horn of every animal, how long it will last, or in the clash between animals, which horn will break. Then, the lifespan of human organs such as the eye and the ear, how long they will remain and when they will stop functioning. All these matters are recorded in Allah's Book of Decree and are included in His knowledge. Allah does not need to make any effort in this regard.

﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ (35:11).

When human thought reflects on these matters and proceeds along these lines, it appears very strange. In connection with this verse, we turn to something to which human thought in general does not turn. Rather, thinking about such matters is not a habit of man at all. It is only the guidance of the Holy Lord that you should reflect in this manner.

Increase in life comes through the number of years and months, and it also comes through blessing in life. Blessing in life means that a person's life is spent in good deeds, and that there is much striving, beneficial work, and deeds and lasting effects. Deficiency in life is similar: either the months and years decrease, or the usefulness of life decreases and its blessing departs, instead of a person doing good deeds his life becomes empty.

Sometimes one hour of life equals an entire lifetime. It is filled with thoughts, awareness and feelings, and within it high-level deeds are carried out and good results emerge. But sometimes a person's entire year passes in emptiness, with no account of it. In Allah's sight that year has no value. All these matters are in Allah's reckoning, and about every existing creature, Allah alone knows all these matters.

Communities are like individuals. Likewise, nations are like a single individual. The same law applies to their lifespan. The lifespan of some increases, while the life of some nation is cut short quickly, and all these meanings are included in this verse. Nations also have a destiny, and they end at Taws wa Rabab (the peacock and the lute, a symbol of worldly luxury and decadence). All things also have a lifespan, just as living things have a lifespan. A rock has a lifespan. A mountain has a lifespan. A river has a lifespan, and a stone has a lifespan, after which it is crushed to pieces. A cave has a lifespan and then it collapses. A canal has a lifespan, and when its lifespan ends the canal dries up and breaks apart. Some things are made by humans. They too have a lifespan. Machines, clothes and all other manufactured products have a lifespan, and after completing their fixed lifespan they break down. All these processes are within Allah's decree, and they are known and predetermined.

If matters are reflected upon from this angle, the study of this universe is seen from a new horizon. This is a new method of studying the universe, and the faculties of human understanding receive a new awareness. A person feels that Allah's power and knowledge are vast, comprehensive and complete. Therefore, with this awareness, a person can never become heedless or astray. Wherever he looks, he sees the craftsmanship of the hand of power, he sees Allah's watchfulness, and he sees the kindness and power of everything.

Now the direction of the discourse turns to one of the cosmic scenes: among the scenes of the waters of the sea, one scene is the varieties of waters. One is sweet water, and the other is intensely salty. The bodies of both kinds of water flow side by side within the sea. Both serve humans, or they do not mix.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 12:

وما یستوی البحرن۔۔۔۔۔ ولعلکم تشکرون (12) The varieties in the creation of water are clear, and the service behind this division is also clear. The use of sweet water is clear. We use it for drinking and for other needs. All kinds of life depend upon water, and water is an essential element of life. As for salt water, such as the sea and the great oceans, some scientists have given amazing information about it and have shown how profound the engineering is in its creation.

And now this cosmic journey concludes with the scene of night and day, the subjugation of the sun and the moon, which is a part of Allah's vast cosmic system.

"For millions of years the earth has been releasing various kinds of gases, and most of these gases are poisonous. But observe the planning of Divine power: the proportion of the air above the earth, within which it is contained, is not affected, and this is necessary for the existence of human beings. The great vehicle of this vast balance is that enormous quantity of water, namely the deep sea, from which life, food, rain, moderate climate and vegetation, and then human life itself, are obtained."

The secrets discovered so far about the creation of water clearly show the wisdom placed in it deliberately. It is clearly apparent that in this creation the Creator has deliberately placed balance and harmony. Upon these harmonies and balances the life of the various things of this universe is established, and the whole system of life stands firm. This intricate system has been deliberately arranged by Allah, Glorified is His Majesty. This balance is so complex and based on such subtle engineering that no intelligent person can think that it has come about by chance. The reference here to two kinds of sea water is intended to show that these waters do not mix with each other; there is a clear distinction between them. This kind of distinguishing separation also exists in human emotions, human consciousness, human inclinations and human values. Then both kinds of water have been made subservient to human beings.

ومن کل تاکلون ۔۔۔۔۔ فیہ مواخر (35: 12) "Yet from both you eat fresh flesh, bring out ornaments to wear, and you see the ships ploughing through them so that you may seek His bounty and be grateful." Fresh flesh refers to fish and the other sea creatures, which are of various kinds, and for adornment, pearls, coral and other gems extracted from the sea. These pearls are found within sea oysters. When grains of sand and water enter inside the oysters, pearls are formed within them through a chemical process. Coral is a animal organism that spreads for miles in the sea, and it grows to such an extent that at times it becomes a danger to sea voyages. Sometimes living creatures also become trapped in its branches. Ornaments were also made from coral, cut in a particular manner.

A ship cleaves through seas and rivers because Allah has placed certain properties in both the water and the ship. The density and structure of the materials from which a ship is built, and the density of sea water itself, are such that the ship floats on the surface of the sea. The same properties have been placed in the winds as well. Then Allah has subjected these forces to human beings, and human beings benefit from them.

لتبتغوا من فضلہ (35: 12) "That you may seek His bounty." Through travel and trade you seek the bounty of Allah. Extract useful things from the sea, and use water and ships for the purposes of transport and conveyance.

ولعلکم تشکرون (35: 12) "So that you may be grateful." Allah has provided you with the means of gratitude. These means are in your hands, and thus Allah is also your helper in rendering thanks.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verses 13–14:

یولج الیل ۔۔۔۔۔ لاجل مسمی

"He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night." These are extremely beautiful scenes. When the night enters the day, the light gradually fades and the darkness slowly spreads. After sunset the darkness deepens further, and the scene of the day entering into the night is also very fascinating. The pale light of dawn appears gradually, the light spreads and the darkness gradually disappears, until the light appears and spreads fully. That is, the night fully consumes the day and the day consumes the night. In both periods the heart finds joy and tranquility, and in both periods the power of a person's reflection becomes sharper. He fears God, because he sees that the God who brings these great phenomena is very great. Thus He draws lines: He pulls one rope and loosens the other. And this system of the alternation of night and day is extremely intricate and delicate; within it there is such stability that not even for a second does any disturbance arise in it, nor does any disorder ever occur in it.

The subjugation of the sun and the moon, and their continuing to run until a appointed term, the term known only to Allah. This is a scene that every human being sees and hears, whether or not he has accurate knowledge of the sun and the moon, and whether or not he has information about the bodies, motion and size of the stars and planets. But these two celestial bodies rise and set before our eyes; they are seen rising and falling before every eye. This movement is a continuous movement, and within it there is not even a moment of disorder, agitation or interval. To see this scene to this extent, no deep knowledge or calculation is required. Therefore the alternation of night and day and the rising and setting of the sun and moon are the scene spread out before our eyes. Today we know somewhat more about them than those people before whom this Qur'an was being revealed.

But the quantity of knowledge is not what matters. What matters is how much we are affected by them, how much our hearts are impressed by them, how much power of reflection is produced within us, and how deeply we perceive Allah's power through this scene. How alive our hearts become through it, because true life is the life of the hearts.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord...﴾ to ﴿...like one who is well-informed (informs you)﴾ (13–14)

This is the Lord who sent winds bearing clouds, who sent rains through clouds, who created you from dust, who made you into pairs, who knows what every female carries in her womb, who knows what the lifespan of each is and what its reduction is, who created the two seas, one sweet and one salty, who created night and day, and who set the courses of the sun and the moon. This is your Lord. Everything belongs to Him.

﴿To Him belongs the dominion. And those you call upon besides Him do not possess [even] a thin membrane of a date seed﴾ (35:13) "And those you call upon besides Him do not even own a thin covering." Qitmir means the thin membrane over a date seed. Even this thin and insignificant covering is not in the possession of those whom you call upon needlessly. A further explanation.

Lesson No. 202: Explanation of the Verses

15 to 26

﴿O people, you are the ones in need of Allah, while Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾ (35:15–17)

When people are invited to strive to come out of darkness into light, and to adopt guidance in place of misguidance, there is a need to remind them of this truth: they are poor and in need of Allah, whereas Allah is completely self-sufficient in comparison to them. When they are invited to faith, to the worship of Allah and to praising Allah, Allah is completely independent of their worship and praise. He is praiseworthy in His own essence and possesses attributes worthy of praise in Himself. Before Allah they have no standing whatsoever. If Allah wills, He can destroy them and bring other people in their place, making them His successors, and what can they do to harm Allah? And this is very easy for Allah.

There is a need for people to be reminded of this truth, so that pride is removed from their minds, the pride by which they think that Allah sends Messengers and arranges their guidance because Allah has some need of our guidance. Allah sends Messengers, and throughout human history they have striven for the guidance of people, bringing them out of darkness toward light.

Allah shows mercy to His servants, bestows His grace and favour upon them, by sending His Messengers to them. These Messengers endure hardships due to the disobedience and harm of the people, and despite this turning away and harm they remain steadfast in the call. Thus, by making this arrangement, Allah bestows pure mercy and kindness upon His servants, because He is Merciful and Generous. These are His essential attributes, not because people can add even the weight of a speck of dust or a particle to Allah's dominion. Moreover, in comparison to Allah, human beings are not a mighty or dominant creation such that Allah cannot replace them. Therefore Allah tolerates their errors. Are these human beings a creation that cannot be replaced? No, that is not the case.

When a person beholds Allah's grace and favour upon himself, he is astonished: on one side is this human being, weak, insignificant and frail, and on the other side is the Divine Being, who is most powerful, and from Him come these mercies upon mankind.

Man is indeed one of the tiniest creatures among the inhabitants of this universe; he lives on a very small sphere among the particles and spheres that revolve around the sun. The sun itself is one of the stars, and the number of stars like the sun is not yet known to man. Other stars appear small, though in their places, at vast distances, they are very great in size, and these great stars float in this space like tiny particles. They are only a very small portion of Allah's creation.

Despite this, man is the recipient of such immense grace and favour from Allah and countless bounties of His. Such mercies have been placed for him upon this earth, deposited within his body, and subjected for his use. Yet despite all this, this insignificant creature goes astray and associates others with Allah, and Allah had to send Messengers for his guidance and direction. One Messenger came after another. Books were sent down upon the Messengers. The Messengers were given miracles that break the normal order. And Allah's grace reached the point where He sent His final Book. In it He recorded the stories of all the Prophets, and recorded the history of the predecessors. Then the capacities given to man and the weaknesses placed within him were all explained in it. Then Allah described the solution to each person's difficulties and removed their hardships.

On one side is this great generosity, and on the other side is the reality that this human being is, in the universe, a small and weak creature. This earth on which he lives is a minor star subordinate to the galaxy of the sun, existing within this vast and terrifying universe of great spheres just as an atom floats in the air of the earth. And Allah, glory be to Him, is the Creator of this whole universe and the heavens. He created this entire universe and all that is in it with a single word. Only His will turned toward it, and by "Be, and it is," everything came into existence, and He is capable of doing so.

It is the duty of people to understand this truth and to reflect on how great Allah's grace is, and to realise that if they are living, they are living only by the grace of Allah and by His great mercy, and this mercy continues despite human denial, turning away and disobedience.

In this respect, this is a deeply intuitive point, and it is also a fact. The Qur'an conveys such truths to human hearts, because when a truth shines upon a person's heart, it transforms that heart completely. All of this is because the Qur'an is the truth, and it has been sent down with truth. Therefore all the matters of the Qur'an are true. It satisfies people with truth and presents reality, and all its indications are entirely true.

Now another point: in this world and the Hereafter, responsibility is individual. Responsibility is individual, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Nor can anyone benefit another. Therefore, if people become guided, this does not fulfil any need of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will be questioned only about his own deeds and duties, while every other individual will be questioned about his own deeds. Each person will be carrying his own burden, and there will be no one to question him about it. If someone adopts a pure life, he does it for himself; he does it for himself and not for anyone else. And on the Day of Resurrection the authority over all affairs will rest solely in the hand of Allah.
