Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 18:

ولا تزر وازرۃ وزرا اخری ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ والی اللہ المصیر (18)

The principle of individual responsibility has a very profound effect on human morality, and it also has a decisive effect on human conduct. It is necessary for a person to develop the awareness that reward and punishment will be based only on his own deeds, and that he will be called to account only for his own deeds. No one will be punished for another's wrongdoing, and he will not be able to escape from his own evil deeds in any way. This is a factor that keeps a person alert at all times, and it also has the benefit that a person does not rely on false hopes that someone will benefit him or that someone will bear a responsibility in his place. This principle is also a source of reassurance for human beings. In it, an individual is satisfied that he will not be held accountable for the evil deeds of the whole community. Thus he will not despair of his own good deeds, provided that he has striven in the community and society for preaching, admonition, enjoining what is good (ma'ruf) and forbidding what is evil (munkar), and has used his strength for this task.

Allah will not call people to account as a group. Rather, every single person will be called to account, and this accountability will cover all of his deeds. It will be within the limits that have been imposed upon him. And it is also an obligation upon every individual to advise others and to carry out the task of their reform to the extent of his ability. If he has discharged this collective responsibility of his, then he will not be responsible for whatever society does. He will receive only the reward of his own good deeds. Moreover, if the community and society are good, but this person is misguided and wicked within it, then the goodness of society will not benefit him in any way, because Allah will not call people to account according to lists.

The Qur'an has stated this principle in accordance with its distinctive mode of expression. This mode has a very profound effect. It is described thus: there are countless people, and each has taken up his own burden. Whoever has a light burden does not carry the burden of another. If someone's burden is very heavy and he calls his closest relatives, no one responds to his call, and no one bears his burden.

This is the scene of a caravan in which every person is carrying his own burden, walking on his own path, until people reach the scale and the one who weighs begins to weigh. Looking at this scene, it appears that every person is under his burden. Someone is weary and exhausted, and someone is light. Every person awaits his own result and is occupied with himself.

Looking at this scene, in which the members of the caravan are weary and exhausted, the address turns toward the Prophet ﷺ.

Innama tunthiru... as-salah (35:18): "You can only warn those who fear their Lord without seeing Him and establish prayer." Warning is beneficial only for such people. Those who fear their Lord although they have not seen Him, and who establish their connection with their Lord by establishing prayer. Such people could benefit from the person of the Prophet and could listen to your words. Therefore, you are not responsible for those who do not fear Allah and who do not establish prayer.

Wa man tazakka fa-innama yatazakka linafsihi (35:18): "And whoever purifies himself, purifies only for his own self." Neither are you responsible for anyone, nor is anyone a guarantor for another. Whoever adopts righteousness and purifies himself, it is he himself who benefits from it. The word (tazakki) contains a very subtle and profound meaning, which includes outward cleanliness, includes cleanliness of heart and consciousness, and includes cleanliness of conduct and attitude. The word (tazakki) carries a deep allusive meaning.

Wa ilallahi al-masir (35:18): "And the return is to Allah." Allah is the Reckoner. He is the One who gives reward and punishment. With Him, a good deed is not lost, an evil deed cannot escape being counted, and the rulings of reward and punishment are not entrusted to people who make concessions in judgment, or who forget, or who simply neglect.

With Allah, belief and disbelief are not equal. The worth of good and evil is not equal. Guidance and misguidance are not equal with Allah. The blind and the sighted are not alike in His sight. Light and darkness do not have the same value there. The benefit of shade and heat is also not equal, and with Allah the living and the dead are not alike. All these things are clearly distinct in respect of value and worth.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran), on Surah 35, verses 19–21:

﴿And the blind and the seeing are not alike; nor are the darknesses and the light; nor the shade and the scorching heat; nor are the living and the dead alike﴾ (35:19–21)

Here, on one side, disbelief, blindness, darkness, heat and death all share a single character, and their meanings are linked to one another. On the other side, faith, light, sight, shade and life also share a single character, and these too are linked to one another.

Faith is light: light in the heart, light in the limbs, light in the senses, a light through which the reality of things is revealed. Values and events become clear, and their limits and connections become evident. The believer sees all things through this light, and he sees events within the light. Therefore his affairs are good, his undertakings are in the right direction, and his feet do not stumble.

Faith is an eye that sees. This eye sees things according to their reality. There is in it neither wavering nor confusion, and the person of faith walks his path in the light, with confidence and with tranquility.

Then, faith is a shade under which a person lives a life of comfort. His self rests in it and his soul is content. From the doubt, restlessness, bewilderment and the scorching heat of the journey through darkness, a person finds refuge in it.

Then, faith is a life: the life of hearts and of consciousness, the life of will, of direction and of orientation. Faith is a movement and a struggle. It is a constructive struggle, a beneficial and purposeful life, in which there is no deadness or lifelessness, and life is never dimmed. In it there is nothing futile and no frivolity.

Disbelief is darkness, and it is many darknesses. When people step out of the circle of the light of faith, they enter various kinds of darkness, darknesses in which the true reality of anything cannot be seen. Disbelief is a kind of harsh sunlight. Within it the heart is caught up in the scorching winds of bewilderment, anxiety, grief, restlessness, wavering and lack of tranquility, and in the Hereafter it falls prey to the heat of Hell.

Disbelief is a kind of death: the death of conscience, being cut off from the source of life, being cut off from the right path, being cut off from the true spring, and being deprived of the true water of life, through which human character is affected. Lesson No. 203: Overview

This lesson consists of an excerpt from the book of the universe and the Book of Allah. The study of the book of the universe is a glance at its beautiful and wondrous pages, which relate to various kinds and various subjects, whose fruits are of many sorts, whose mountains are of many colours, and whose humans, animals and creatures that walk upon the earth are diverse in type and form. This wondrous study of the beautiful universe is very interesting, and the whole universe is its subject. Then there is the study of the revealed Book of Allah, its teachings and truths, and its confirmation and affirmation of the books revealed before it; then the Muslim Ummah being made the heir of the previous nations and the ranks of those heirs; and the forgiveness, pardon and rewards prepared for the believers; the scenes of Paradise and the scenes of Hell and the conditions of the disbelievers; and, at the end, the resolution that all of this occurs in accordance with Allah's knowledge.

Lesson No. 203: Explanation of the Verses

27 ... to ... 38

Alam tara anna Allaha ... inna Allaha Azizun Ghafur (27–28)

This is a glimpse of the universe. It is shown that the source of the Book of Allah and the source of the book of the universe is one. In this glimpse the whole earth is displayed and the colours and designs of the whole earth are manifested. The colours and varieties of fruits, the colours and types of mountains, the colours and forms of people, and the kinds and varieties of animals and cattle: within a few words the features of the entire earth have been contained, enveloping living and non-living things alike. Within a few words the picture of this display of the All-Holy Lord has been drawn, which is very captivating, and these captivating features are spread across the whole earth.

At the beginning we see that rains are falling, and as a result of these rains, multicoloured fruits come into being on this earth. Here, since the display of various colours is intended, instead of mentioning the fruits, their colours are shown.

Fa-akhrajna bihi thamarati mukhtalifan alwanuha (35:27): "And through it We bring forth fruits of varying colours." The colours of fruits are in truth a great exhibition hall, and no part of the colour scheme in it could be produced even if all the painters of the world combined. The colour of one kind of fruit differs from other kinds. Rather, even within one kind of fruit there are different colours, and one shade differs from others. And the colour of each grain also differs from the others.

After the colours of fruits, then the colours of mountains. Between the colours of fruits and the colours of mountains there appears to be no apparent connection, but if a real study and research is undertaken, a natural connection exists. There is a kind of connection between the colours of mountains and the colours of fruits. Indeed, the colours of stones and mountains sometimes resemble the colours of fruits.

Wa-min al-jibali judadun ... wa-gharabibu sud (35:27): "And among the mountains are streaks, white and red of varying shades, and extremely dark black." Judad means paths and streaks, that is, bands. The verse says that the "judad bid" (white streaks) also vary in colour, and likewise the "judad hmr" (red streaks) vary in colour. That is, each kind, namely white and red, also varies in colour, and some streaks are intensely black.

Here attention is drawn to the fact that stones of one colour, for example red and white, differ among themselves. These varying colours of mountains and stones are mentioned after the varying colours of fruits. This produces movement in the human heart and sharpens the sense of beauty. Thus beauty and loveliness are presented here in the form of abstract art, which at the same time attracts the sense of sight in stones and also draws the sense of sight in fruits, although there appears to be no relation between fruits and stones. But abstract aesthetic sense perceives beauty everywhere, and this characteristic of the Qur'an deserves attention.

Then the colours of people: this is not limited to the common colours of humans; rather, there is difference in colour and build among people of the same colour, and even two real brothers differ in colour. Beyond humans, there are the colours of birds, cattle and beasts. Dabbah is the term applied to every animal that walks on the earth. An-am is used for camels, cows, sheep and goats. After the word dawab, the special mention of an-am is made because humans are more familiar with them. The colour scheme of these is also astonishing, like that of fruits and stones.

This album of the colours of the universe is wondrous and strange. The Qur'an turns its pages and draws the human being's attention to contemplate this cosmic colour scheme with a seeing eye. Only people of knowledge and taste can enjoy it and derive lessons from it. Only people of knowledge can, by attaining wisdom and the power of Allah, reflect on the greatness of Allah and fear Him.

Innama yakhsha Allaha min ibadihi al-ulama (35:28): "Indeed, it is only those among His servants who have knowledge that truly fear Allah." The pages of the book of the universe that the Qur'an has turned are very few of its pages, and the scholars are in fact constantly reflecting on this universe. Therefore it is the scholars who in truth possess real knowledge of Allah. They are more aware of the signs of Allah's attributes, and they perceive the recognition of Allah through the signs of His power. They have awareness of Allah's greatness by seeing the wonders of His creation. This is why they truly fear Him. They worship Him genuinely out of fear of Him. The awareness of these scholars of the universe concerning Allah is not a vague or confused awareness, but they possess deep recognition of Allah.

These pages of the Qur'an are a sample of the Book of Allah, while colours and other cosmic wonders are a sample of this universe, and their reality is in fact acknowledged only by the scholars of the universe. Those who possess true knowledge of the Book and also true knowledge of creation, who have direct recognition of Allah: knowledge which is the awareness of their heart and through which their heart is moved, through which they can see well the beautiful colours of this universe, derive joy from them, and study the perfect power of Allah.

In the composition and creation of this universe, the element of beauty and loveliness is the principal aim, and the perfection of this beauty is that every thing performs its natural duties through its natural beauty and loveliness. These flowers, by their beauty and their very pleasant fragrance, draw bees and butterflies towards themselves. The duty of the bees and butterflies with respect to flowers is that they bring about pollination between female and male flowers so that fruit forms on the plants. Thus these flowers accomplish this work through their beauty and loveliness. Between female and male, beauty becomes a mutual attraction, and in this way the two sexes perform their respective appointed and natural functions. Thus all things perform their natural duties through beauty and loveliness. Therefore beauty is intended for its own sake in the scheme of this universe, and this is why the Book of Allah, to manifest the beauty of the book of the universe, everywhere attracts human sight.

Inna Allaha Azizun Ghafur (35:28): "Indeed, Allah is All-Mighty and Forgiving." He is Mighty, who created these things and is able to give reward and punishment. He is Ghafur, and He forgives those who fall short in obeying Him and in fear and awe of Him. Moreover, He forgives those who do not reflect on the wonders of Allah's handiwork.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verses 29–30:

Now the direction of address turns from the pages of the universe to the pages of the Book of Allah, to show what those who recite it have before them and what blessings have been prepared for them.

"Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hope for a commerce that will never perish. That He may pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative." (35:29–30)

By the recitation of the Book is meant something other than merely repeating its words mechanically or silently. It is reciting the Qur'an with reflection (tadabbur), through which the reader perceives a truth and is moved by it. After that, he acts upon it and shapes his life according to it. This is why, after the recitation of the Qur'an, the establishment of prayer (iqamat al-salah) and spending (infaq) are mentioned, whether done secretly or openly. Then such people are given hope that in this bargain they will suffer no loss. Such people have the recognition (ma'rifah) that what is with Allah is better than what is with them. They also have the certainty that they are engaged in a trade whose profit is secure and guaranteed. They are dealing with Allah alone, and a transaction made with Allah is exceedingly profitable. This is a trade of the Hereafter, in which the rate of profit is very high. It is a trade in which the exchange is completely full and exact, and upon which there is also the bounty of Allah. He (is Ghafur and Shakur) forgives shortcomings and is most appreciative. The meaning of Allah's appreciation (shukr) is that Allah gives the best reward; but the word shukr is used for encouragement, and this statement is made to induce shame and modesty in man: when Allah, the true Benefactor, shows appreciation to His servants, then it is the duty of the servants to remain at all times engaged in the praise of Allah.

After this, there is an indication of the nature of this Book: within it there is nothing but truth, and its inheritors will be the inheritors of the Gardens. Further on, the discussion of the inheritors of this truth is coming.

Rather, this Book is the page of the universe that is read, and the whole universe is a page that is silent and is observed. ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾. The Muslim Ummah should reflect upon these words. Allah has bestowed upon it a very great honour, and He has placed upon its shoulders a very great responsibility. Through this selection there falls upon it the obligation that this Book has its requirements. Is this chosen Ummah listening to what the Qur'an says, and fulfilling its responsibilities? Allah has indeed given this Ummah great honour because of this selection, and then, by appointing reward and recompense for it, He has further bestowed excellence upon it.

﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾. The first group will be greater in number, therefore it is mentioned first. These people will be those who wrong themselves, and among them the evil deeds will outweigh the good deeds, and their good deeds will be few. The second group will be the moderate (muqtasid), that is, those who keep to the middle course. Their good and bad deeds will be equal. The third group will be the foremost in good deeds (sabiq bil-khayrat), that is, those who race ahead in good deeds. Their good deeds will far outweigh their bad deeds. However, the grace of Allah will encompass all three of them. All these people will be included among the blessings mentioned in the verses that follow, although they will differ in their ranks.

We do not wish to add anything to what the Qur'an has said regarding the nobility of the Ummah, because Allah has chosen this Ummah and has announced for it a good recompense. The verses themselves show that the final outcome of the Ummah will be this: the entire Ummah will reach a good end, and we leave its details to Allah. We here set aside the reward which Allah has decreed for these three kinds of people of this Ummah, and it will certainly be a good reward.

This scene describes solid, material blessings and psychological comforts that are felt and perceived. Here is their outward appearance.

"They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk" (35:33). This adornment is material, solid and visible. The human soul loves such things, and besides them there will be the pleasure of Allah, inner contentment, and peace and tranquility.

They say: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us all grief" (35:34). "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us." And this world, where every person is beset by anxiety, restlessness, calamities and difficulties, is in comparison with the Hereafter a place of grief, whereas there will be enduring bliss. The anguish of the Day of Gathering will be greater than the worldly troubles, and from it they will have found deliverance.

"Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative" (35:34). "Indeed, our Lord is All-Forgiving and All-Appreciative." He has forgiven us, appreciated our acceptable deeds, and given a very great reward for them.

The Qur'anic phrase: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence by His bounty﴾ (35:35) — "Who has settled us in the abode of permanence (dar al-muqamah) by His bounty." It means He made us dwell there forever and we became permanent residents. He did this through His grace and generosity, because we were not entitled to it by our deeds. It is a favour: no hardship afflicts us there, nor does fatigue overtake us, rather there is comfort, tranquillity and every kind of blessing gathered together.

The whole atmosphere is filled with ease, comfort and blessings. And for this soft and delicate, pleasant setting, Allah has also chosen words that are extremely gentle and delicate. Even the word ḥuzn (grief) has been made gentle here by being mentioned as ḥuzn, and the term dar al-muqamah has been used for Paradise. About fatigue and hardship it is said that it will not even be able to touch us. And the rhythm of the words and phrases is itself extremely delightful, like a very gentle music.

Now, turn to the other side! Anguish, restlessness, distress and turmoil.

"And those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell; they shall not be decreed to die, so that they die, nor shall its punishment be lightened for them." Neither this, nor that. For them there shall be no death either.

﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful disbeliever.﴾ (35:36)

And now our ears hear a harsh and rough sound. It is a clamour that rises from many voices combined; it is an outcry coming from various directions, from those who have been thrown into Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35 (Fatir), verse 37:

Wa hum yastarkhūna fīhā... min naṣīr (37): "They will cry out therein..."

Wa hum yastarkhūna fīhā (35:37): "They will cry out therein, saying..." The meaning is already embedded in the pronunciation of the word (yaṣṭarikhūn) itself. The harsh sound alone reveals its meaning. What do they say?

Rabbanā akhrijnā... naʿmal (35:37): "Our Lord, bring us out from here, so that we may do righteous deeds, unlike those we used to do before." Now they are bowing before Allah, confessing their sins and filled with remorse, but when

the birds have eaten the field (i.e., too late). Listen to how harsh and blunt the reply is, one that also carries rebuke.

Awalam nuʿammirkum... min naṣīr (35:37): "(They will be told:) Did We not give you a lifespan in which one who wished to take a lesson could take it? And a warner had also come to you. Now taste (the punishment). The wrongdoers have no helper here." We gave you a lifespan; you did not benefit from it, although that lifespan was sufficient for those who wished to receive admonition. Then, for your further facilitation, prophets were also sent. They warned you, but you were not frightened. In these verses two mutually contrasting states are described. On one side there is peace and comfort; on the other, anguish and restlessness. On one side there is the sweet melody of thankfulness for blessings; on the other, screaming and wailing. On one side there is honour, respect and welcome; on the other, neglect and reproach. On one side there are gentle, delightful words; on the other, harsh and severe rebuke. Thus there is complete contrast in both aspects of the speech, in every single part. And at the very end, a final comment on all the scenes comes, especially on the people of faith being chosen and given honour, and the Ummah of Muṣṭafā (ﷺ) being favoured.

Indeed, Allah is Knowing of the unseen of the heavens and the earth; indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts. (35:38)

Allah's complete, all-encompassing and vast knowledge is stated after the subjects in which it was said that Allah revealed the Book, and those who were named as its inheritors were chosen above the peoples of the worlds. If some of them commit wrongdoing or shortcoming, Allah will forgive them. This will be a favour and grace from Allah upon them, and then the end described for the people of disbelief. This is the final comment upon all these realities: that He is the Knower of the unseen, and He knows everything existing in the heavens and the earths. He knows even the matters within hearts, and therefore He will make all decisions through this great, complete and all-encompassing knowledge. There will be no injustice in Allah's decisions.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 39:

Lesson No. 204 At a Glance

This is the final lesson of this surah, and it consists of a wide-ranging journey of observation. Throughout it, the heart and mind are sharply stirred, and signs and guidance are given. The journey stretches far across the long valley of human history, in which there are countless ups and downs. Some nations and peoples are present, and some are not. Then there is a journey through the heavens and the earth, in which, despite great effort, no partner or equal of Allah was found. The whole universe was searched. Then there is a journey for the purpose of contemplating how Allah holds the heavens and the earth, and what the delicate balance is that prevents these gigantic spheres of the universe from colliding with one another. Then there is a journey through the valleys of a people who rejected guidance, although before this they used to pray that if a Messenger came to them, they would be more guided than either of the two nations. But when a Messenger, a bearer of glad tidings and a warner, came to them, they forgot their promise and began to feel intense aversion toward the Messenger they had longed for. And then there is a tour of the nations destroyed throughout the long valleys of human history, who were overtaken by punishment and perished, yet people today take no lesson from these calamities. And then the frightening conclusion of this lesson.

(Allah says) ﴿And if Allah were to seize people for what they earned, He would not leave upon the earth a single moving creature﴾ (35:45). But it is a great favour of Allah that He grants people respite and does not send down destructive punishment upon them, although they deserve it.

Lesson No. 204 Explanation of the Verses

Verses 39 to 45

﴿He it is who made you successors upon the earth. So whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon himself. And the disbelief of the disbelievers increases them in nothing but loathing from their Lord; and the disbelief of the disbelievers increases them in nothing but loss﴾ (35:39).

The coming and going of generations upon the earth, their continuity, the passing away of one generation and another taking its place, the ending of one dominion and the establishment of another, one blazing flame being extinguished and another being kindled, one nation vanishing and another rising to prominence, and this happening for centuries: reflection upon this course of history gives a person much lesson and admonition, and the present nations think that they too will be annihilated in the same way. Those who come after will examine their traces just as we examine the traces of those who have passed. Thus even the most heedless person can come to his senses. Thus a grave-digger can reflect upon what the hand of power is, whose wondrous works these are: that one's life is short and another's long; today one government exists and tomorrow another; today one country is held by one occupier and tomorrow by another; one people succeeds another people. Everything is in motion. Its end is approaching, and what remains is only the name of Allah, which neither ceases nor has an end.

That which is departing, and whose existence comes to an end, is not everlasting. Its example is like a traveller who halts at a station; tomorrow he must move on, and those who come later see what he did and what he left behind. And the outcome is that his account will be taken of what he did and what he failed to do. Therefore it is the duty of every person to do good deeds in his brief life and to leave behind a good remembrance, and to do things that will benefit him in his resting place. These are some of the thoughts that leap over the walls of the heart and mind, especially when one beholds the rise and fall of nations, contemplates the rising and setting, and reflects upon the affairs of powers that ascend and powers that vanish, and sees one people inheriting another.

﴿He it is who made you successors upon the earth﴾ (35:39). Under the shadow of this powerful, continuous and observable scene, people are reminded that responsibility is individual. Therefore on the Day of Resurrection no one will be able to bear another's responsibility, and no one will be able to defend against another. Here it is indicated that just as you turn away, just as you disbelieve, just as you become entangled in error, in the end the outcome will be most abominable.

﴿So whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon himself, and the disbelief of the disbelievers increases them in nothing but loathing from their Lord; and the disbelief of the disbelievers increases them in nothing but loss﴾ (35:39). The meaning of maqt is intense wrath, and one upon whom Allah's intense wrath falls should know how dire a fate awaits him. What greater loss could there be?

The second journey is through the vastness of the heavens, so that it may be ascertained whether there are any traces of the achievements of those whom they associate with Allah in the heavens and the earth. In the heavens and the earth there is no trace of them whatsoever, nor any sign.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 40:

قل ارءیتم۔۔۔۔۔ الا غرورا (40) “۔

This argument is entirely clear, and this proof does not need any lengthy explanation. The earth, and whatever is within it, is the creation of Allah, and this sky, to its furthest expanses, belongs to Allah. Among the things visible on this earth, which one is there that anyone other than Allah could claim, or that could be claimed on behalf of someone else, to have created it? If anyone makes such a claim, then every thing will cry out against his claim that it is false, and every thing will proclaim loudly that it was created by Allah. Every thing carries within itself such signs that they are sufficient to refute the claim of any claimant, because these signs bear no resemblance to any human craftsmanship. That is to say, the things that humans have made do not possess the qualities of the products of the system of divine power.

ام لھم شرک فی السموت (35: 40) “Or do they have a partnership in the heavens?” This is rejected all the more so. When they have no share in anything of the earth, how can they have a share in anything of the heavens? For when no one can claim that any thing of the earth is the creation of these so-called beings, how can anyone claim that any thing of the heavens is? In short, these gods have neither a share in the creation of anything in the heavens nor a share in the dominion. Whatever you name, not even the jinn and the angels have any such status. Their belief was that the jinn steal news of the heavens and bring it, and that they learn these reports from them. But their belief was never that the jinn or the angels are partners with God in the heavens.

ام اتینھم۔۔۔۔ بینت منہ (35: 40) “Or have We given them a book from which they derive authority?” The supposition that Allah has given these self-made gods some scripture, and that they are certain that they are partners with God, is also false. Here, according to this interpretation, the interrogation may also be directed not at the partners but at the polytheists: that is, is the blind faith these people hold in these self-invented deities based on some scripture from Allah that was revealed to these polytheists, from which they take their belief and derive their arguments? This is not correct, and they cannot produce any such scripture. Here, according to this interpretation, there is also an indication that beliefs are established only through a book from Allah and a clear textual authority, and that only the Book of Allah can be the source for doctrines, because it is the certain fountain of guidance. Since they have no explicit textual proof, their claim is false. Against them stands the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whose every word is what Allah has commanded. Why then do these people turn away, when the correct way to take beliefs is precisely that these people obey the words of the Messenger ﷺ?

بل ان یعد۔۔۔۔ الا غرورا (35: 40) “Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.” These wrongdoers make grand and sweeping promises to one another that their path is this path, the path of their forefathers, and that in the end they will prevail. Yet these people are deceived and deluded. Some of them deceive others. They live in that pride, and this is not a state that benefits them.

After the statement that there is no partner with Allah, neither in the heavens nor in the earth, it is shown that it is the work of His power that holds the earth and the heavens, and that He alone, without any partner, is the manager and sustainer of this universe. Instead of seeking some other deity in the universe, look at Him Himself.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease [moving]. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ (35:41) Look at this sky, look at the earth, and look at the countless billions of celestial bodies scattered across this boundless expanse. All of them remain in their places, moving within their orbits, fixed in their courses. They do not deviate from them, nor does their speed suffer any disturbance. They cannot leave their orbits, nor can their speed become slower or faster. Yet there is no pillar set up to keep them in their places in this way, nor are they bound by strong ropes. Nothing apparent supports them. Look at this great creation, which exceeds billions and trillions in number and is extraordinarily wondrous. The eyes of a wise person must surely be opened to the fact that behind it works the power of a Mighty Lord of the Worlds, whose hand holds this great system together.

If these stars of the heavens and the earth were to be dislodged from their places and scattered in disorder, no one could set them in order again. This is the time when the Resurrection will take place, and for the end of this world the Qur'an has declared the disruption of this very system to be the sign, when mountains and stars will fly away like tufts of wool, and every thing in this cosmic system will collide with another. This is the appointed time in which the reckoning and accounting of all people will take place, and what each person did in the world will be called to account. The end of this world will be followed by the Hereafter, and this other world will be entirely different from this one in its nature and temperament.

This is why the following remark is made about the holding up of the heavens and the earth:

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ (35:41). He is Forbearing (al-Halim). He gives people respite; He does not destroy this world because of their evil conduct, nor does He begin calling them to account before the appointed term. He gives people the opportunity to repent and grants them time to prepare for the Day of Resurrection. And He is Forgiving (al-Ghafur) in such a way that He does not call people to account for every crime they committed; rather, Allah pardons a large portion of people's wrongdoings. Whenever Allah sees any good in them, He forgives them. This is a guidance that warns people to regard this opportunity and need as a treasure, for if they squander this chance, it will not return.

The fourth journey concerns the condition of the people of Makkah and the polytheists around them. These people used to pray that if Allah were to send a Messenger among them and reveal a Book to him, they would believe. Then they broke their covenant and committed corruption on the earth. They are warned that there is no change in the Sunnah of Allah, and the Sunnah of Allah does not change.

﴿And they swore by Allah...﴾ to ﴿...never will you find any change in the way of Allah﴾ (42–43).

The Arabs saw that the Jews lived among them in the Arabian Peninsula, that a Book had been given to them, and that these Jews had deviated from their religion and were without action. The Arabs also read their history, that they had killed many of their own Messengers, and that whenever truth came to them they turned away from it. At that time, considering themselves greater than the Jews, they used to swear oaths that if Allah sent them a Prophet, and he were raised up among the Arabs, they would be more rightly guided than all the nations of the world. Their intention was that they would be more upon guidance than the Jews. These people were pointing towards the Jews.

﴿...if a warner had come to them, they would have been better guided than any other nation﴾ (35:42). This was their condition before the mission, and this was their belief. The Qur'an presents this belief to them in such a way: just recall this situation, what you used to say. After this, the circumstances that actually occurred after the arrival of the Messenger are presented before them.

﴿But when a warner came to them, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ to ﴿...the evil of plotting﴾ (35:42–43). ﴿...due to arrogance on the earth and evil plotting.﴾ How evil it is that a person swears that his conduct will be such, and then he adopts the opposite conduct, out of arrogance and pride and because of his evil schemes. The Qur'an records the real cause of their denial, and after this the Qur'an gives its judgment and response regarding their deceptions: what will be the faith of one who commits such a repugnant act, and what will be his end.

﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own planners﴾ (35:43). That is, their evil plots will turn against themselves, and these evil plots will bewilder them, and their deeds will be lost. The stories of the earlier nations that befell them are known to them. They are merely waiting for the firm Sunnah of Allah to seize them.

﴿Then you will not find any change in the Sunnah of Allah...﴾ (35:43) ﴿...and you will never find that the Sunnah of Allah can be turned from its appointed course by any power.﴾

The affairs of people are not proceeding by chance, nor have this life and these creatures on this earth been created in vain. This world has certain laws that never change. The Holy Qur'an confirms this reality and teaches people that they should not regard the events of this world as isolated occurrences, nor should they pass their lives heedless of these divine Sunan, nor limit their lives to the briefest moments and places of time and space. The Qur'an wishes to elevate their outlook and connect the patterns of their lives with the patterns of this universe. Accordingly, the Qur'an repeatedly draws attention to the fact that Allah has established unchanging principles in this universe. It keeps directing them to the events that occurred in this world in accordance with these divine Sunan, and it demonstrates that the past of mankind shows that these Sunan operate in this universe. This fifth journey is one example of that. Here too, after saying that the Sunan of Allah do not change, attention is drawn to this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 44:

أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا... عَلِيمًا قَدِيرًا (44)

Travelling through the earth should be done with open eyes and an awakened heart and mind, and the events of earlier peoples should remain before one's view: what they used to do and what their end was. It is essential that fear of God and lessons-giving signs settle into human consciousness and heart from the events and calamities of the earth.

This is why the Qur'an repeatedly gives the guidance that you should travel through the earth and study the stories of the rise and fall of nations, and observe the days and nights of the destroyed peoples, whose name and trace have been wiped from this earth. Take a lesson from them and awaken those hearts that lack knowledge. If there is knowledge, there is no feeling in them, and if there is feeling, they do not take heed. In these dead hearts there is no awareness of the Sunan Ilahiyyah (the divine laws of history, sunan), and they do not interpret historical events in the light of the Sunan Ilahiyyah. Yet the only difference between a human being and an animal is that a human interprets events and explanations in the light of principles, whereas an animal does not think at all about circumstances, events, principles, rules and the Sunan Ilahiyyah; it does not derive rulings or conclusions from any event. It should also be kept in view that all of humankind are alike before the Sunan Ilahiyyah and the laws of nature (nawamis al-fitrah).

In this historical journey, the Qur'an places the audience at the ruins of the destroyed nations of history and reminds them that these people were possessed of great power and splendour, and that their power and splendour did not save them. Therefore, there exists a power superior to all powers: a power to which no power is comparable, and which no power can overcome. This power can seize these people in the same way that it seized earlier nations.

﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِن شَيْءٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ (35:44) "And Allah is not one to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth." And upon this comes the commentary that explains it and presents the proof:

﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَلِيمًا قَدِيرًا﴾ (35:44) "Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent." At the very end comes the conclusion of the Surah, in which the bounties, forgiveness and forbearance of Allah are also expressed, and the awareness of Allah's power and might is also made to be felt. And it is explained that the respite Allah is granting people is granted because He is Merciful and Generous, and that Allah adopts a gentle attitude in reckoning and accounting.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 35, verse 45:

ولو يؤاخذ الله... بعباده بصيرا (45)

People who disbelieve in Allah's blessings, commit corruption on the earth, and engage in oppression, transgression and arrogance, their conduct is extremely evil. If Allah were to seize people for this evil conduct immediately, the reach of Allah's seizure would extend across the entire globe, and this whole globe would cease to be fit for life. It would not remain habitable only for humans; not a single living thing would remain here. This manner of expression shows that what people do is very bad and abominable, and if Allah were to seize them immediately for it, the natural and moral consequences of people's deeds would lead to their swift ruin. But Allah is Forbearing (Halim), and He does not hasten to seize people.

ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى (35:45) "But He gives them respite until an appointed term." That is, He gives every individual respite until the natural span of their life, and in the world they complete their lifespan. He also grants respite to societies and nations until their appointed time, until they are destroyed and vacate the place for other nations, and He grants respite to all of humankind; when the appointed time arrives, He will establish the Resurrection and take account. In this way He gives people the opportunity that perhaps they may do good deeds.

فإذا جاء أجلهم (35:45) "Then when their term comes..." When the time for earning and acting is complete and the time of reckoning arrives, Allah will not wrong them.

فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا (35:45) "Indeed, Allah is ever Seeing of His servants." Allah's seeing His servants is a guarantee that He will carry out a complete reckoning of their deeds in accordance with their actions. Nothing of their deeds, minor or major, will be left out. This is the final note of this surah. Its beginning was praise of Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who

جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة (35:1) "...makes the angels messengers having wings..." and who brings His message from the heavens to the earth, containing glad tidings and warning. The glad tidings are of Paradise and the warning is of Hell. Between this beginning and this end, the surah has taken readers on countless journeys through the study of this entire universe. This is the conclusion of those journeys. This is the end of life and this is the end of the human being.
